comments.body:
## CORRECTION — the title's claim is NOT supported by the evidence I filed it on

I filed this asserting blame auto-derivation "is usually wrong". **I conflated two different
things**, and the distinction destroys the claim:

- **What I actually had:** each agent's analysis of what `git blame` on the *implicated lines*
  would name. That is a hand-run blame over specific line ranges.
- **What the ticket asserts:** that `caused_by` **auto-derivation** — a different mechanism, which
  `docs/clone-guidance.md` describes as blaming *files* over the ticket's impacted paths — produces
  wrong origins.

I never observed the second. I inferred it from the first.

## The direct evidence points the OTHER way

`rebar transition` has **no `--caused-by` flag** (`brokendown-moonlit-kiskadee`,
`0276-7eea-baf0-48e3`), and unknown flags are silently ignored. So on four closes today where the
flag was passed per the `/rebar-debug` protocol, it did nothing and **the real auto-derivation ran**.
In every observed case it attached an edge pointing at **the same origin the agent had proven by
hand**.

That is four out of four where the fallback agreed with a proven attribution. It is a small sample
and the closes were not chosen to test this — but it is *direct* evidence about the actual
mechanism, where my original table was *indirect* evidence about a different one.

## What survives, and what does not

**Does not survive:** the assertion that the fallback is usually wrong. Withdrawn. The title is
wrong and should be read as the question it should have been.

**Survives, and is still worth investigating:**

- The **defect shapes** in the original table are real and were each proven: unmet obligations,
  carrier commits, and omissions dominated this session's root causes. Those shapes are genuinely
  hard to attribute, and hand-run `git blame` on the implicated lines misled in several of them.
  That much stands on its own evidence.
- Whether the file-level auto-derivation copes with those shapes **is now an open question with
  evidence on both sides**, which is a better ticket than the one I filed.
- The distinguishability question is untouched by the correction: a blame-derived edge and a
  supplied one are indistinguishable on read, so the metric cannot weight them differently even if
  someone measures the error rate.

## Why this matters beyond tidying a ticket

A ticket asserting a conclusion in its title shapes what an implementer looks for. Left as filed,
this one would have sent someone hunting for evidence that the fallback is broken — and there is a
real risk they would have found it, because the shapes ARE hard and a motivated search over 2,400
tickets will surface examples. The measurement has to be able to come back "the fallback is fine".

Retitling accordingly and rewriting the acceptance criteria so the ticket asks rather than asserts.
The `--caused-by` gap must be fixed FIRST, or the measurement is confounded: while the flag is
silently ignored, *every* edge is blame-derived regardless of what the closing agent believed, so
there is no "supplied" population to compare against.

comments.body:
## Second correction — the counter-evidence in my retraction was itself wrong

My retraction argued the thesis was undermined because "the flag never worked, so blame ran on all
four closes anyway — and landed on the same origin the agent had proven by hand."

**The flag DOES work** (verified: `_parse_flags` at `_commands/transition.py:123-124,164`, the
passing CLI interface test at `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_caused_by_autoderive.py:33`, and a
peer's demonstration in a store with zero commits where blame could not have produced anything). So
on those closes the edges came from the **flag**, not from blame. Blame very likely never ran.

**That specific counter-evidence is void.** I have no observations of the file-level auto-derivation
agreeing with a proven origin, because I never observed it running.

## What the ticket should say, now that both of my errors are subtracted

The **original retraction still holds, for its original reason**: I conflated each agent's
hand-run `git blame` over *implicated lines* with the `caused_by` auto-derivation, which
`docs/clone-guidance.md` describes as blaming *files* over impacted paths. Those are different
mechanisms and I only ever observed the first. That conflation is what makes "usually wrong" an
unsupported claim, and it is unaffected by the flag question.

So: the title should ask, not assert — which is how it now reads. But the evidence base is now
**neither for nor against**. I have no direct data on the auto-derivation's accuracy in either
direction, and this ticket should say so plainly rather than carry my second wrong story.

The **defect shapes** in the original table remain proven and remain the reason the question is
worth asking: unmet obligations, carrier commits, and omissions dominated this session's root
causes, and hand-run blame misled on several of them. Whether the file-level fallback copes with
those shapes is exactly what has not been measured.

One consequence for the measurement design: since `--caused-by` works, there **is** a distinguishable
"supplied" population after all, so the `depends_on` link to `brokendown-moonlit-kiskadee` is no
longer a hard prerequisite — that ticket is now a P3 help-text fix, not a blocker. Reduced to
`relates_to` unless a future reader disagrees.

Three position changes on one question is more than this deserved. The durable lesson is the one
that caused all three: **I twice reasoned from an experiment that did not exercise the code path in
question** — a stale working tree, then a no-op transition — and both times the error was caught by
someone else re-deriving rather than by me.

comments.body:
## Measurement findings: is `derive_caused_by` reliable for this codebase's history?

All numbers below were produced in worktree `work-50e3` (HEAD at current `origin/main`) with the
worktree `.venv` interpreter, read-only against the live tracker and full git history.

### Method (reproducible)

**Step 1 — population.** Reduce every ticket directory under
`rebar.config.tracker_dir(repo_root)` with `rebar.reducer.reduce_ticket`; select
`ticket_type == "bug"`, `status == "closed"`, with ≥1 active `caused_by` dep. Result:
**782 bugs total, 760 closed, 88 closed bugs carrying a `caused_by` edge** — the whole
population, no sampling.

**Step 2 — re-run the real deriver on each.** For each of the 88, call the actual mechanism and
annotate abstentions with the observable failure reason:

```python
import os, json
from rebar import config
from rebar.metrics.blame import derive_caused_by, _find_fixing_commit
from rebar._engine_support import field_reads
repo_root = os.getcwd(); tracker = str(config.tracker_dir(repo_root))
for r in population:               # the 88 closed bugs with caused_by edges
    derived = derive_caused_by(r["id"], repo_root, tracker)
    if derived is None:
        fixing = _find_fixing_commit(repo_root, r["id"], tracker)
        if not fixing: reason = "no-fixing-commit"
        elif not [p for e in field_reads.file_impact(r["id"], tracker)
                  if (p := (e or {}).get("path"))]: reason = "no-file-impact"
        else: reason = "no-majority-or-unresolvable"
    # classify: derived in r["targets"] → agree; else disagree; None → abstain
```

### Result — population bound (n = 88)

| classification | n | share | abstain-reason breakdown |
|---|---|---|---|
| agree (derived ∈ recorded) | 38 | 43% | — |
| disagree (derived ∉ recorded) | 6 | 7% | — |
| abstain (derived = None) | 44 | 50% | no-majority-or-unresolvable 33, no-file-impact 8, no-fixing-commit 3 |

As the plan requires, this table is a **bound, not a supplied-vs-derived identification**: the
recorded edge carries no provenance marker (`_apply_caused_by` writes via `_write_link_event`
with no derived-vs-explicit field — src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py), so "agree" means
only *consistent with* blame-derivation, and disagree/abstain means *not reproducible by the
deriver today* (history drift is a live confounder: 3 fixing commits no longer resolve, 8
tickets carry an edge but no file_impact path the deriver can blame, and reformat/move carriers
landed since close can dissolve a majority that existed at close time).

Notable structure in the 6 disagreements: **5 of the 6 share the same recorded target**
(`ed5c-42fc-bb7f-4cf4`, "No guard makes an unsigned, identity-less writer loud") with five
*different* derived targets — a batch attribution of a guard-gap bug family to one origin
ticket, exactly the many-bugs-one-cause shape where per-bug file blame scatters. None of those
five tickets' prose independently proves the ed5c attribution, so they are excluded from the
accuracy subsample below, but the cluster is direct evidence that when a *family* of bugs is
attributed to one origin, the deriver would have scattered the attribution across unrelated
tickets had the edges not been supplied.

### Result — accuracy against proven origins (subsample n = 8)

Ground truth: the ten attributions this ticket's original description table established under
`/rebar-debug` (each with a proven mechanism), plus `aragonite-bleached-vipersquid` (17c3),
whose root-cause comment names `789c-1251-fc21-4cf6`. Two of the ten are outside the
population (`steep-tired-whimbrel` carries no caused_by edge today;
`nonodorous-snotty-seaurchin` was proven unattributable, so correctly has no edge). For the
remaining **8**, every recorded edge matches the proven origin (they were supplied per the
debug protocol). The deriver's score against that ground truth:

| bug | proven origin | deriver today | verdict | defect shape |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bediasite-bilineate-stoat | cec6-0a0e | None (no-majority-or-unresolvable) | abstained | omission at origin (single commit — blame *was* predicted correct; drift since) |
| perkish-balsamic-pupfish | fc20-2df1 | None (no-majority-or-unresolvable) | abstained | unmet obligation (fc20 never touched gates.py) |
| irongrey-chubby-oxpecker | 789c-1251 | None (no-file-impact) | abstained | unmet obligation (consumer vs producer contract) |
| moist-short-lionfish | c1de-d6a0 | **e1f4-d518** | **wrong-target** | unmet obligation — named exactly the innocent producer the original table predicted blame would name |
| electronic-deducible-maggot | 8d36-a15a | None (no-file-impact) | abstained | carrier commit (June file-move) |
| itchy-arbored-peccary | b73c + 615c | None (no-majority-or-unresolvable) | abstained | omission (ADR promise no AC obliged) |
| ruling-magnific-bats | 555e-3efa | None (no-majority-or-unresolvable) | abstained | cause site IS fix site (blame predicted correct; drift since) |
| aragonite-bleached-vipersquid | 789c-1251 | None (no-majority-or-unresolvable) | abstained | unmet obligation (789c moved decode composition one side only) |

**Correct 0 / wrong-target 1 / abstained 7.** On the only bugs where ground truth is
independently proven, the deriver reproduced **none** of the correct attributions, and the one
time it spoke confidently it named the innocent party — the producer whose code was correct
when written (`e1f4` wrote `pending_enrichment` for drain-time enumeration; `c1de` put it on
the write path under a self-declared 20 ms budget). The proportion of blame-derivable edges in
this subsample naming a defensibly wrong origin is therefore **1/1 of its confident outputs**
(and 1/8 of the subsample; the other 7 fail closed).

### Decision (a): should a blame-derived edge be distinguishable on read from a supplied one? — YES

This measurement is itself the strongest evidence: with 88 edges and no provenance field, the
central question "how many of these are guesses?" is **unanswerable** — the study could only
bound it (38 consistent-with-blame vs 50 not-reproducible-today). Every consumer of the edge
(escape-rate lenses, the epic-close `caused_by` floor, any future reviewer) inherits that
ambiguity. A `derived: blame | explicit` marker on the link event would cost one field at
write time and make the metric's confidence computable. Filed as a proposal ticket
(discovered_from this one) for operator adjudication — not implemented here.

### Decision (b): should the fallback decline to attribute for shapes it cannot get right? — Keep fail-closed as-is; do NOT add shape detection; discount rather than delete

Reasoning from the numbers:
- The fallback **already declines** in the hard cases: 50% abstention on the population, 7/8 on
  the proven subsample. The strict >50% majority rule is doing exactly the fail-closed work the
  design intended, and the dominant shapes here (unmet obligation, carrier, omission) mostly
  land in abstention, not misattribution.
- The residual risk is the confident-but-wrong case (moist-short-lionfish; plus the ed5c
  cluster's scattered would-be targets): when the shape is "consumer edited last, producer
  innocent", file-majority blame returns a confident wrong answer *by construction*, and no
  mechanical signal inside blame distinguishes it — the deriver cannot know the defect shape
  without understanding the mechanism, which is precisely what the human/debug protocol
  supplies. So "decline for shapes it cannot get right" is not implementable as stated: shape
  is not observable to the mechanism.
- The implementable version is decision (a): mark derived edges, and let consumers weight or
  exclude them (e.g. metrics report supplied-vs-derived escape rates separately). That
  preserves the 38 agreements (harmless where blame is right, e.g. single-commit omissions)
  while quarantining the guesses. A behaviour change to the deriver itself is NOT recommended
  on this evidence.

### Limitations (named, per plan)

- **History drift:** the deriver ran today, not at close time. Abstentions include cases blame
  may have answered (possibly correctly) at close — bediasite and ruling-magnific-bats were
  predicted blame-correct and now abstain. The 0/8 correct figure is therefore a *today* figure;
  it understates close-time accuracy by an unknown amount, but the wrong-target case is
  drift-independent (e1f4 was the wrong answer then and now).
- **Agreement is a bound:** with no provenance marker, the 38 agreements cannot be split into
  "blame agreed with a proof" vs "blame agreeing with itself".
- **Subsample bias:** the 8 proven origins all come from one session's `/rebar-debug` work and
  over-represent the hard shapes (that session is why the question was asked). They are the
  only ground truth available, not a random sample.
- The verdict is correspondingly scoped: **the fallback's fail-closed behaviour is working; its
  confident answers are unverifiable in bulk and were wrong when verifiable; the missing piece
  is provenance, not a smarter guesser.**

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`caused_by` auto-derivation falls back to best-effort `git blame` over a bug's impacted paths
when no `--caused-by` is supplied (`derive_caused_by`, invoked from
`_commands/transition_close.py::_resolve_caused_by_culprit` only when the bug carries no
`caused_by` edge yet). The edge feeds `rebar metrics`' escape-rate lenses and the epic-close
`caused_by` floor, and a WRONG edge is worse than an absent one: it silently charges an escaped
defect to a ticket whose reviewers could not plausibly have caught it.

Whether the file-level auto-derivation is accurate for this codebase's dominant defect shapes
is an OPEN QUESTION with no direct evidence either way — see the two correction comments
below. The proven part is only that the dominant defect shapes here (unmet obligations,
carrier commits, omissions) are structurally hard for blame. This ticket measures rather than
asserts.

## Approach

Measure the actual mechanism (`derive_caused_by`) against the actual store, read-only:

1. **Enumerate the population.** Reduce every ticket in the tracker; select closed `bug` tickets
   whose reduced state carries at least one active `caused_by` edge. Report the population size.
2. **Re-run the real deriver on each.** For every sampled bug, call
   `rebar.metrics.blame.derive_caused_by(bug_id, repo_root, tracker)` in this worktree (full
   git history, current HEAD) and compare its output to the recorded edge target:
   agreement / disagreement / abstention (`None`). Because the recorded edge carries NO
   derived-vs-explicit marker (`_apply_caused_by` writes via `_write_link_event` with no
   provenance field — verified at src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py), this
   classification BOUNDS rather than identifies the blame-derived population, and the
   findings must say so: agreement means only "consistent with blame-derivation";
   disagreement/abstention means "not reproducible by the deriver TODAY", which is evidence
   of explicit supply but not proof, since the deriver also abstains or diverges for reasons
   unrelated to supply (fixing commit no longer resolving, `file_impact` paths renamed or
   deleted, majority dissolved by later reformat/move carriers, culprit trailer no longer
   resolving). Each non-agreement case is annotated with the deriver's observable failure
   reason (no-fixing-commit / no-file-impact / no-majority / unresolvable-culprit /
   different-target) and reported as a bound with those caveats.
3. **Score accuracy against proven origins.** For the subsample of bugs whose ticket record
   independently establishes the true origin (a root-cause comment or description naming the
   introducing ticket — the `/rebar-debug` protocol writes these), compare the deriver's output
   to that proven origin and classify each case: correct / wrong-target / abstained. Classify
   each wrong/abstained case by defect shape (unmet obligation / carrier commit / omission /
   other) so the rate connects to the shapes hypothesis.
4. **Record the two decisions** the measurement informs, with reasoning, as a findings comment:
   (a) should a blame-derived edge be distinguishable on read from a supplied one;
   (b) should the fallback decline to attribute for shapes it cannot get right.
   Any resulting schema change or review-time criterion is FILED as its own ticket linked
   `discovered_from` this one — gate/criterion changes are operator-adjudicated, so those
   tickets are proposals for the operator, not work performed here.

Default assumptions (stated so no executor question remains): the sample is the WHOLE
population of closed bugs with `caused_by` edges; a proven origin exists only where the ticket
record names one explicitly; history drift counts as a named limitation, not an error, when
the deriver abstains for lack of the fixing commit.

## Scope

No repository file changes: measurement scripts run ad-hoc in the worktree interpreter against
the store and git history; results, methodology, and decisions are recorded on this ticket.
Follow-up implementation work (schema marker, deriver behaviour change, review criterion) is
filed as separate tickets, not done here.

## Testing / Verification

The deliverable is a measurement, so verification is reproducibility: the findings comment
must quote the exact probe snippets run (Python importing
`rebar.metrics.blame.derive_caused_by` and `rebar.reducer.reduce_ticket`, executed with this
worktree's `.venv` interpreter against the live tracker and git history) together with their
raw counts, so any reader can re-run the same snippet and reproduce the
agreement/disagreement/abstention table. The proving command for each numeric claim is that
quoted snippet; the proving evidence for each decision is its recorded reasoning referencing
those numbers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [non-codebase] The rate is measured, not estimated: the population of closed bugs with
      `caused_by` edges is enumerated (size reported), the real `derive_caused_by` is re-run on
      each, and the agreement/disagreement/abstention counts are reported in a findings comment
      on this ticket, with the method stated — checked by reading the comment.
      provenance: environment=work-50e3 worktree venv, live tracker and full git history at origin/main; principal=RebarBotNava analysis agent; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the real derive_caused_by ran on all 88 population bugs; the findings comment quotes the snippet and raw counts (agree 38 / disagree 6 / abstain 44).
- [x] [non-codebase] For every bug in the subsample with an independently proven origin, the
      deriver's output is scored correct / wrong-target / abstained and classified by defect
      shape; the proportion of blame-derivable edges naming a defensibly wrong origin is
      reported with the subsample size — checked by reading the comment.
      provenance: environment=work-50e3 worktree venv, ground truth from the store's root-cause records; principal=RebarBotNava analysis agent; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the deriver's real output on each of the 8 proven-origin bugs was scored: correct 0 / wrong-target 1 / abstained 7, each shape-classified in the findings table.
- [x] [non-codebase] A decision is recorded on whether a blame-derived edge should be
      distinguishable from an explicitly supplied one on read, with reasoning — checked by
      reading the comment.
      provenance: environment=work-50e3 worktree; principal=RebarBotNava analysis agent; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=static-analysis — the YES decision follows from the verified absence of a provenance field at the _write_link_event call sites in transition_close.py plus the measured 38/6/44 bound; recorded in the findings comment.
- [x] [non-codebase] A decision is recorded on whether the fallback should decline to attribute
      for the shapes it cannot get right, rather than guessing, with reasoning — checked by
      reading the comment.
      provenance: environment=work-50e3 worktree; principal=RebarBotNava analysis agent; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=static-analysis — the decision (keep fail-closed as-is; shape is unobservable to the mechanism; discount via the provenance marker) is recorded in the findings comment with the 50% population and 7/8 subsample abstention figures.
- [x] [non-codebase] Any proposed review-time criterion or schema change is filed as its own
      ticket linked `discovered_from` this one rather than implemented here — checked by the
      links on this ticket.
      provenance: environment=work-50e3 worktree, live tracker; principal=RebarBotNava analysis agent; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — proposal ticket highborn-gabardine-dairycow (6536-367c-e358-424d) was created and linked discovered_from this ticket; nothing was implemented (operator-adjudicated).

compiled_state.title: Measure whether caused_by blame auto-derivation is reliable for this codebase's dominant defect shapes
